payload.root_cause: tag_orders uses a mutable default argument (existing: list = []) and aliases it via `result = existing` (pyshop/reports.py:23-25). The default list is created once at function definition time and shared across all calls that omit `existing`, so every call appends to the same persistent list. The first call tag_orders(ORDERS, 'gift') appends 'o1','o3' to the shared default; the second call tag_orders(ORDERS, 'rush') appends 'o3' to that same list, returning ['o1','o3','o3'] instead of a fresh ['o3'].

payload.rationale: The root cause is the classic mutable-default-argument bug: `existing: list = []` creates one shared list at function definition time, and `result = existing` aliases it, so every call without an explicit `existing` appends to that same persistent list (first call leaves ['o1','o3'], second call returns ['o1','o3','o3']). Replacing the mutable default with a `None` sentinel and building `result` as a fresh list (copying `existing` when provided) eliminates the shared state. Each call now starts from a new list, so `tag_orders(ORDERS, 'rush')` correctly returns ['o3'], while passing `existing=['o0']` still yields ['o0','o3'] per the documented append-to-existing behavior.
